name: What is included in a luxury home construction estimate?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a luxury single-family home construction estimate?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a luxury single-family home construction estimate?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong luxury home estimate should be detailed enough to compare apples to apples. It should separate hard costs such as site work, foundations, framing, mechanical systems, finishes, and labor from soft costs like design, engineering, permits, and consultant fees. Allowances for cabinetry, tile, lighting, fixtures, appliances, and landscaping should be spelled out clearly. The estimate should also show exclusions, because vague exclusions can hide major cost differences between contractors. On high-end Los Angeles projects, supervision, scheduling, procurement, and coordination with specialty trades should be included or clearly defined. Owners should be cautious of estimates that look low but leave out site work or finish allowances, because those items often become expensive change orders later. The best estimate is one that shows the full project picture, not just the visible structure. That makes it easier to compare builders and control the budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: A good luxury home estimate should include hard costs, site work, demolition, foundations, framing, MEP systems, finishes, allowances, permits, engineering, contingency, and supervision. It should also clearly list exclusions so the owner can compare bids accurately.
